description:
# Subagent status via bw substrate: universal heartbeat + read-before-write discipline

## Empirical anchor

2026-05-12 ariadne PLINY incident. PLINY dispatched CAPTAIN_ADA via `Agent({ run_in_background: true, ... })` to author a synthetic corpus (~400 tickets). PRINCIPAL asked PLINY "is ADA stuck?" while ADA was mid-execution. PLINY had no in-band mechanism to introspect ADA's running state. PLINY confabulated "I never made the Agent tool call" — falsely — because PLINY couldn't verify dispatch state from its own context and asserted instead of saying "uncertain, checking." PRINCIPAL caught the confabulation via the Claude Code Desktop Tasks pane (UI-only introspection). Diagnostic surfaced two distinct gaps: (1) no in-band status surface for dispatched Agents, (2) confabulation under uncertainty (filed separately as the confabulation-discipline ticket).

PRINCIPAL's structural insight: bw IS the answer. We already have a durable, searchable, shared substrate. The dispatched agent heartbeats progress via `bw comment` on its dispatch ticket; the orchestrator reads bw to know status. This is "cooked into the DNA" of every agent rather than relying on Anthropic's tool surface (which does not currently expose mid-execution Agent introspection).

## The discipline

Two halves, asymmetrically implemented but symmetric in user-visible behavior:

### Half 1 (upward — CAPTAIN → orchestrator): heartbeat via bw at every state milestone

Every CAPTAIN dispatch follows this canonical comm contract:

1. **At dispatch entry:** `bw comment <dispatch-ticket> "<seat> activated on <ticket>. Reading brief + role file."`
2. **At every state transition** (phase boundary, sub-phase entry, major discovery, blocker identified, etc.): `bw comment <dispatch-ticket> "<one-line state>"`.
3. **At completion:** `bw comment <dispatch-ticket> "<verdict>: <brief summary>. Returning."` BEFORE returning the tool result.
4. **If heads-down longer than 10 minutes without a state transition:** post a pull-heartbeat ("still working on X, no state change yet") to maintain the check-in cadence floor.

Heartbeats are the canonical status surface. The orchestrator does not poll the agent's introspection (no clean tool for that); the orchestrator reads the heartbeats.

### Half 2 (downward — orchestrator → CAPTAIN): read-before-write at every yield point

Every `bw comment` write by a CAPTAIN is preceded by a `bw show <dispatch-ticket>` read. The read picks up any new comments from the orchestrator (or peer CAPTAINs) since the last check. The CAPTAIN addresses anything tagged `[for: <CAPTAIN>]` or otherwise actionable BEFORE proceeding to the next state.

This is co-operative-multitasking-shaped — the CAPTAIN voluntarily yields at write points; those yields are the only mid-execution interruption surface. The pattern produces effective bidirectional comms with bw as the medium:

- A chatty CAPTAIN (writing often) is automatically a responsive CAPTAIN (checking often)
- A heads-down CAPTAIN respects the 10-min pull-heartbeat floor, so the maximum check-in lag is bounded
- The orchestrator's "downward push" is actually a "CAPTAIN-side pull on next yield" — but it works as if it were push because yields happen at every state milestone

### Cooperative yield is the only mid-execution interruption surface

The orchestrator CANNOT push-interrupt a running CAPTAIN. The only hard-abort is `TaskStop`. So the CAPTAIN's yield discipline is structurally load-bearing — without it, the orchestrator has no way to redirect a mid-flight CAPTAIN short of killing it. The role files MUST encode the yield discipline; it cannot be left to ad-hoc cleverness.

## Phase-A architectural decisions (LOCKED for whatever arc picks this up)

### A1. bw is the canonical status surface — LOCKED

Anthropic's tool surface does NOT provide mid-execution Agent introspection (and structurally cannot without overflowing context with the agent's JSONL transcript). The substrate's answer is to use bw — a substrate we already control — as the shared status channel. This is fixed.

### A2. CAPTAINs do not fire Monitor — LOCKED

CAPTAIN-tier agents are short-lived (one Agent invocation), their chat dies when they return, and they cannot `TaskStop` what they spawn (per [issue #23154](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/23154) — subagents can't run TaskStop). Firing `Monitor` from inside a CAPTAIN would orphan the Monitor; its notifications would land in a dead conversation; the spawned process would leak. CAPTAIN role files prohibit `Monitor` (and any `run_in_background: true` Bash) from inside a CAPTAIN dispatch.

### A3. Heartbeat cadence floor: 10 minutes — LOCKED at this default, overridable per-dispatch

CAPTAINs that go heads-down without natural state transitions post a pull-heartbeat at least every 10 minutes. Per-dispatch override allowed when the engagement justifies it (e.g., a long generative compute with documented expected duration).

### A4. Read-before-write is mandatory, not optional — LOCKED

Every `bw comment` write by a CAPTAIN MUST be preceded by a `bw show` read of the dispatch ticket. This is the canonical yield-and-check pattern. Skipping the read breaks bidirectionality and means the CAPTAIN can drift out of sync with orchestrator guidance.

### A5. CAPTAIN-side `Monitor` and `run_in_background` Bash both forbidden — LOCKED

Both are orphan-bug surfaces in the CAPTAIN tier. Background work belongs to the orchestrator. If a CAPTAIN genuinely needs background-style compute, the orchestrator dispatches it and the CAPTAIN's verdict references the background output via bw.

## Substrate touch-points

Files this discipline lands in:

1. **`substrate/operating-disciplines.md`** — new section on "Subagent status via bw." Canonical universal-seat answer to "where is my dispatched agent?" is "read bw comments on the dispatch ticket." Includes the four-bullet heartbeat-and-read discipline + the cooperative-yield framing.

2. **`substrate/CAPTAIN_VERA.md`** — new subsection in §5 (disciplines specific to this seat): heartbeat discipline + read-before-write + Monitor-forbidden + background-Bash-forbidden.

3. **`substrate/CAPTAIN_CATO.md`** — analogous subsection in §6.

4. **`substrate/CAPTAIN_ARGUS.md`** — analogous subsection in §6.

5. **`substrate/CAPTAIN_ZENO.md`** — analogous subsection in §6.

6. **`substrate/CAPTAIN_STRABO.md`** — analogous subsection.

7. **`substrate/CAPTAIN_ADA.md`** (if present; otherwise wherever ADA discipline lives) — analogous subsection. ADA is the seat most likely to have long heads-down generative work, so the pull-heartbeat-floor matters most here.

8. **`substrate/CAPTAIN_DAEDALUS.md`** — analogous subsection.

9. **`substrate/CAPTAIN_HERALD.md`**, **`substrate/CAPTAIN_BARTLEBY.md`**, **`substrate/CAPTAIN_CURATOR.md`** (and any other CAPTAINs in substrate) — analogous subsection.

10. **`substrate/MAJOR_PLINY.md`** — orchestrator-side guidance: monitor via bw on dispatch tickets; rely on CAPTAIN heartbeats as the canonical status surface; do not poll agent introspection.

11. **`substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md`** — analogous guidance for pair-programming-mode CAPTAIN dispatches.

12. **Any agent-author template / skill** — the canonical heartbeat-and-read discipline becomes the default new-CAPTAIN scaffold; new CAPTAINs inherit the discipline rather than re-deriving it.

## Gauntlet shape

Full gauntlet — DAEDALUS + ARGUS + ADA + VERA + CATO + ZENO. Substantive substrate-prose update across ~10+ role files plus operating-disciplines + agent-author template. ~200-300 LOC of prose. Identical shape to Arc 23. ARGUS audit is load-bearing because the discipline lands across many files and must be self-consistent.

## Cross-references

- **Ticket B (orchestrator-side: Monitor + bw bridge):** complementary; orchestrator-side push mechanism. Ships together with this ticket.
- **Ticket C (confabulation discipline):** same empirical anchor (2026-05-12 ariadne incident); different failure mode (verb-level discipline, not comms architecture). Ships in same arc but independent.
- **stoa--nax:** redundant-checks + N=1 — related substrate-discipline cluster.
- **stoa--148:** CATO empirical-env reproduction — related verifier-side hygiene.
- **stoa--ivc:** radio-check pattern — Monitor-on-bw is the canonical transport for the radio-check; this ticket sharpens existing radio-check wording.
- **stoa--ay1:** adaptive polling cadence — related; the 10-min pull-heartbeat-floor cooperates with adaptive-cadence framing.

## Sequencing

P2. Substrate-DNA discipline. Lands in a future arc (Arc 24+) AFTER Arc 23 (`stoa--pmp`) closes — same PLINY seat can't be doubly-dispatched. Probably bundled with Ticket B + Ticket C as a single "comms-hygiene arc."

NOT folded into Arc 22 (`stoa--jru`) — Arc 22's directive at `arc-22-build-directive.md` is already locked at 512 lines and scope-creeping it late introduces defects. Cleaner to ship Arc 22 as-is, then new arc bundles these three.

## Out of scope

- Implementing Anthropic-side tooling for Agent introspection (not our substrate)
- Forking Claude Code (gratuitous; the bw bridge is sufficient)
- Replacing `Monitor` with a custom poll mechanism (Monitor is the right tool on the orchestrator side; the issue is just CAPTAIN-side prohibition)
- Auto-orphan-cleanup scripts for the issue-#23154 bug (out of substrate; OS-level concern)

## Authorship attribution

Authored by Denson Smith via POLYBIUS conversation, 2026-05-12. All edits to substrate land under Denson Smith authorship.

comments.text: Discipline-cadence recalibration per PRINCIPAL 2026-05-12: pull-heartbeat-floor changed from 10-min default to **60-min default**. Long generative work (corpus authoring, deep design, multi-file refactor) needs a relaxed minimum; 10 min was over-engineering. Override per-dispatch still allowed — orchestrator may tighten to 10-min or loosen further when the engagement warrants. Empirical anchor: 2026-05-12 ariadne ADA factory-corpus generation, pre-Windows-restart. PRINCIPAL's framing: 'I want to be able to get her to report in at least once per hour.' A3 amended to read: 'Heartbeat cadence floor: 60 minutes — LOCKED at this default, overridable per-dispatch. CAPTAINs that go heads-down without natural state transitions post a pull-heartbeat at least every 60 minutes. Per-dispatch override allowed (tighter for short engagements, looser only with documented expected duration).'
